ing: or crab legs cut in pieces
such as Scotch bonnet, left whole, optional
st: Rinse the leaves well, then chop them roughly. Slice the okra and chop the onion, scallions, and garlic.
Melt [[2 tbsp]] butter in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onion, scallions, and garlic for 4 minutes until soft.
Add the okra, thyme, and the [[4 cups]] broth. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir in the chopped leaves and the whole hot pepper if using. Cover and simmer for 15 minutes until the leaves are very tender (spinach needs only 5 minutes).
Take out the thyme stems and hot pepper. Blend the soup with an immersion blender, or in batches in a blender with the lid vented, until mostly smooth.
Return to low heat, stir in the coconut milk, [[1 tsp]] salt, and the pepper. Warm gently for 5 minutes without boiling hard.
Add the crab meat and heat through for 3 minutes. Taste and adjust the salt.
Ladle into bowls and serve hot with bread or boiled root vegetables.
Whisk [[2 cups]] flour, the baking powder, [[1 tbsp]] sugar, and [[0.5 tsp]] salt in a large bowl.
Rub the cold butter into the flour with your fingertips until it looks like coarse crumbs.
Add the water a little at a time, mixing until you have a soft dough that is not sticky. You may need a bit more or less than [[0.75 cup]].
Knead for 2 minutes until smooth, cover the bowl, and let the dough rest for 20 minutes.
Divide into 8 balls and flatten each into a disc about 1/2 inch thick.
Heat the oil in a deep skillet to 350°F (175°C), or until a pinch of dough sizzles right away.
Fry a few bakes at a time for 2 to 3 minutes per side, until puffed and golden brown, turning once.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with butter, cheese, or saltfish.

ing: such as whitebait or small anchovies, rinsed
st: Rinse the tiny fish in cold water and drain well. If they are salted, soak them in water for 15 minutes first, then drain.
Mix [[1 cup]] flour, the baking powder, [[0.5 tsp]] salt, and the pepper in a bowl.
Stir in the onion, garlic, chili, thyme, and scallion.
Add the water gradually, whisking until you have a thick batter that falls slowly off a spoon. You may not need all [[0.75 cup]].
Fold the fish gently into the batter.
Heat the oil in a deep skillet to 350°F (175°C).
Drop heaping tablespoons of batter into the oil, a few at a time, and fry for 3 to 4 minutes, turning once, until deep golden and crisp.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm with hot sauce or lime.
Put the salt cod in a pot, cover with water, and simmer for 15 minutes. Drain, cover with fresh water, and repeat once more to remove the salt. For milder fish, soak overnight instead.
Drain the fish, let it cool a bit, then flake it into pieces and remove any bones or skin.
Cut a shallow slit down the length of each green banana skin. Boil in water with [[1 tsp]] salt for 20 to 25 minutes, until tender when poked.
Drain the bananas, let them cool a few minutes, then peel off the skins and cut into thick slices.
Heat [[3 tbsp]] oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion, bell pepper, garlic, and scallions for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the tomatoes, thyme, hot pepper, and black pepper and cook for 5 minutes until saucy.
Stir in the flaked fish and cook for 5 minutes. Taste before adding any salt, as the fish may still be salty.
Serve the saltfish hot with the boiled green bananas alongside.

ing: or sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
st: Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and brown the beef in batches for about 8 minutes total.
Add the onion, garlic, scallions, and thyme and stir for 2 minutes.
Pour in [[8 cups]] water, add [[1 tsp]] salt and the pepper, and bring to a boil. Reduce to a simmer, cover, and cook for 1 hour 15 minutes until the beef is almost tender.
Peel and cube the dasheen and yams. Peel the green bananas by cutting off the ends and slicing through the skin.
Add the dasheen, yams, carrots, and green bananas to the pot. Simmer for 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, mix [[1 cup]] flour with [[1 tsp]] salt, then stir in [[0.5 cup]] water to make a firm dough. Roll small pieces into spindle-shaped dumplings.
Drop the dumplings into the soup and simmer 12 to 15 minutes until cooked through.
Mash a few pieces of dasheen against the side of the pot to thicken the broth. Taste, adjust the salt, and serve hot.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Have four clean crab shells or small ramekins ready.
Melt [[2 tbsp]] of the butter in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion, scallions, garlic, and chili for 4 minutes until soft.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the thyme, [[0.5 tsp]] salt, and the pepper.
Mix the crab meat, the onion mixture, [[0.5 cup]] of the breadcrumbs, and the juice of the lime in a bowl, folding gently so the crab stays in pieces.
Spoon the filling into the shells, mounding it slightly.
Melt the remaining [[2 tbsp]] butter, stir it into the remaining [[0.5 cup]] breadcrumbs, and sprinkle over the top.
Bake on a baking sheet for 15 to 20 minutes until hot and golden on top.
Serve hot with extra lime wedges.
